newsitem.title: SWEDEN: H&M shares tumble on bourse list move.
newsitem.headline: H&M shares tumble on bourse list move.

text.p: Shares of Swedish fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz (H&M) fell on Thursday when the company announced it was planning to move its shares from Stockholm bourse's main A list to the smaller O list.
H&M shares were trading at 257 crowns before the announcement but fell as low as 231 crowns on the news.
The stock recovered slightly and at 1015 GMT was trading 18 crowns lower at 236 crowns.
"Overseas portfolio administrators cannot own O-listed shares without special permission," said one broker.
"Really it is only foreigners and Stefan Persson and family that own the company."
He expected overseas interests to sell the stock heavily in afternoon trade.

Another broker was sceptical about the decision to move the shares which is designed to avoid a new tax law under which owners of family-owned firmed traded on the A list will pay a higher wealth tax.
"It does not look good...The key owner is doing this just so that he himself can earn more money and it does not help Sweden overseas," he said.
